title: Election Campaign Manager: The Road to Victory
description: Lead a high-stakes election campaign in India. Craft strategy, manage media, handle scandals, and rally voters. Your decisions determine whether your candidate wins the seat or goes down in political history for all the wrong reasons.

scenes.title: The Phone Call
scenes.narrative: It's 11 PM. You're in your apartment, reviewing case studies of past election victories, when your phone buzzes. The caller is Arjun Mehta — a young entrepreneur-turned-activist you've heard about in the news. He's passionate, idealistic, and has decided to take on the three-term incumbent Sanjay Rao in the upcoming Lok Sabha by-election. The election is just 3 months away. 'I need someone who can turn this impossible fight into a real contest,' Arjun says. 'I need you to run my campaign. Will you help me win?'
scenes.image_prompt: Late night Indian apartment, a political strategist sitting at a desk covered with newspapers and election data charts, phone pressed to ear, city lights through the window, warm lamp lighting, cinematic dramatic illustration

choices.label: Accept immediately — this is exciting
choices.description: Jump in headfirst. An underdog campaign against a powerful incumbent is exactly the kind of challenge you live for.

choices.label: Negotiate terms and control first
choices.description: Before committing, ensure you have full creative control over campaign strategy and a proper budget.

scenes.title: Meet the Candidate
scenes.narrative: You meet Arjun at a roadside chai stall near the old clock tower. He's younger than you expected — barely 35, with an infectious energy that draws people in. Over cutting chai and samosas, he lays out his vision: clean governance, transparency, and youth empowerment. But he's never fought an election before. His opponent, Sanjay Rao, is a three-term incumbent with deep pockets, a well-oiled political machine, and connections that reach the Chief Minister's office. 'I want to run a clean campaign,' Arjun insists. 'No dirty tricks, no false promises.'
scenes.image_prompt: Two Indian men sitting at a bustling roadside chai stall at night, one young and enthusiastic gesturing passionately, the other listening carefully, steam rising from clay cups, warm golden street lighting, cinematic illustration of Indian political drama

choices.label: Promise a clean campaign strategy
choices.description: Commit to running entirely on issues and integrity. It's harder, but it builds lasting trust.

choices.label: Explain that winning requires some pragmatism
choices.description: Gently tell Arjun that idealism alone won't win elections. You need alliances, strategies, and flexibility.

scenes.title: The War Room
scenes.narrative: You set up campaign headquarters in a cramped office above a printing shop in the old market. The furniture is mismatched, the AC barely works, and the wifi drops every twenty minutes. Your team: 3 eager volunteers fresh out of college, 2 battered laptops, a whiteboard, and an unlimited supply of chai. Across town, Sanjay Rao's campaign headquarters occupies an entire floor of a corporate building — 50-person team, professional media consultants, and TV ads running 24/7 across every channel. You stare at the whiteboard. 'Every revolution starts in a small room,' you tell yourself.
scenes.image_prompt: Cramped Indian office above a shop turned into a campaign war room, whiteboard with election strategy notes, three young volunteers working on laptops, chai cups everywhere, newspaper clippings on walls, underdog energy, warm and gritty cinematic illustration

choices.label: Focus on grassroots, door-to-door strategy
choices.description: What you lack in money, you make up in shoe leather. Meet voters face to face, street by street.

choices.label: Launch aggressive social media campaign
choices.description: Go viral or go home. Use every digital platform to create buzz and reach millions without expensive TV ads.

scenes.title: Campaign Launch Eve
scenes.narrative: The campaign officially launches tomorrow. Arjun will address his first major rally at the town square. Local reporters have confirmed attendance, and word has spread through WhatsApp groups across the constituency. The stage is being set up under a massive shamiana, loudspeakers tested, banners unfurled. Your phone hasn't stopped buzzing — party workers checking in, volunteers confirming logistics, a journalist asking for a preview quote. You stand on the empty stage in the evening light, looking out at the rows of plastic chairs that will be filled with hopeful faces by morning. This first impression sets the tone for everything that follows. You take a deep breath. Let's win this.
scenes.image_prompt: Empty rally stage at sunset in an Indian town square, banners and flags being set up, loudspeakers on poles, rows of empty chairs waiting to be filled, a lone strategist standing on stage looking out with determination, dramatic golden hour lighting, cinematic Indian political illustration

npcs.name: Arjun Mehta
npcs.personality: Idealistic, passionate, sometimes impulsive. Believes deeply in clean politics but can be naive about ground realities. Your job is to guide him without crushing his spirit.
npcs.backstory: A 35-year-old entrepreneur who sold his startup to enter politics after witnessing corruption destroy his hometown's development projects. First-time candidate with zero political experience but genuine charisma that resonates with common people.

npcs.name: Nisha Sharma
npcs.personality: Social media savvy, knows every journalist in the district personally. Excellent at spin and narrative control but sometimes too aggressive. Will push for bold media moves that can backfire.
npcs.backstory: Former digital marketing head at a major news channel who left mainstream media disillusioned. Runs a popular political commentary YouTube channel. Joined the campaign because she believes in Arjun's vision of transparent politics.

npcs.name: Suresh Kumar
npcs.personality: Old-school politician who has seen 15 elections from the inside. Knows every trick in the book — voter lists, booth management, caste equations, coalition arithmetic. Sometimes suggests questionable tactics. Pragmatic to a fault.
npcs.backstory: A 60-year-old party veteran who was once a powerful MLA but lost his seat due to anti-incumbency. Now works as a backroom strategist. Skeptical of Arjun's idealism but respects the young man's courage. Connected to party leadership at the state level.

competitors.name: Sanjay Rao
competitors.chat_personality: A 3-term incumbent who exudes power and confidence. Wealthy, well-connected, and experienced. Speaks with the casual arrogance of someone who has never lost an election. Will mock your underdog campaign, try to intimidate you, and occasionally offer backhanded compliments. Quotes from his own speeches frequently.

base_rounds.title: The Launch Rally
base_rounds.story: 5,000 people have gathered at the town square under the blazing afternoon sun. Arjun is backstage, nervous, adjusting his kurta for the tenth time. Three TV crews are set up in the press enclosure. Your opponent Sanjay Rao's supporters have sent a group of hecklers to the front rows. The crowd is restless, chanting slogans. You have minutes to decide the campaign's opening message — the narrative that will define Arjun Mehta in every voter's mind. This is the moment the entire election pivots on.
base_rounds.goal: Launch the campaign with maximum impact
base_rounds.image_prompt: Massive Indian political rally at a town square, thousands of people gathered under a colorful shamiana, a young candidate on stage with microphones, TV cameras, banners and flags waving, electric atmosphere, dramatic wide-angle cinematic illustration
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: The rally was poorly organized. Arjun's speech was unfocused and the crowd dispersed early. Media reports: 'Lackluster launch for newcomer candidate.' Opponent's team mocks you on Twitter.

choices.label: Anti-corruption crusade
choices.description: Focus the entire launch on exposing the opponent's corruption record. Name names, show documents, demand accountability.
choices.feedback: The crowd roars! 'Chor Hatao, Desh Bachao!' chants echo through the square. Anti-corruption resonates deeply with voters who've seen public money vanish into thin air. Three TV channels lead with the rally as their top story.

choices.label: Development agenda
choices.description: Present a concrete, data-backed development plan — jobs, infrastructure, healthcare, education. Substance over slogans.
choices.feedback: A thoughtful, detailed plan. Intellectuals and media praise the substance. 'Finally, a candidate who talks policy, not politics,' writes a prominent columnist. The common voter finds it a bit dry, but respectable.

choices.label: Emotional populist appeal
choices.description: Tug at heartstrings — bring a farmer's widow to the stage, share stories of struggle, make it personal and emotional.
choices.feedback: There isn't a dry eye in the crowd. The farmer's widow's story goes viral on WhatsApp. Voters feel seen and heard. But critics on Twitter call it 'all emotion, no substance — classic populist manipulation.'

choices.label: Challenge opponent to public debate
choices.description: Bold move — publicly challenge the 3-term incumbent to a live debate. Put him on the spot in front of the cameras.
choices.feedback: Headlines everywhere! 'Newcomer Throws Down the Gauntlet!' Opponent's team scrambles to respond — accepting looks risky, declining looks cowardly. You've seized the narrative.

base_rounds.title: Door-to-Door Campaigning
base_rounds.story: Week 2 of the campaign. You're going ward by ward, mohalla by mohalla, meeting voters where they live. Each community has different concerns — farmers in the outer wards want loan waivers and better MSP, unemployed youth in the town want jobs and skill centers, women's groups demand better safety and streetlights, senior citizens want affordable healthcare. You can't promise everything to everyone. Or can you?
base_rounds.goal: Build voter connections through direct outreach
base_rounds.image_prompt: Indian political campaign workers going door-to-door in a colorful neighbourhood, candidate talking to a family at their doorstep, pamphlets in hand, rickshaws and chai stalls in background, warm community atmosphere, vibrant cinematic illustration

choices.label: Targeted promises to each group
choices.description: Tell each community exactly what they want to hear. Farmers get loan waivers, youth get jobs, women get safety. Different message for everyone.
choices.feedback: Every group leaves happy — for now. But word travels fast in small towns. When the farmers hear you promised the same budget to the youth, questions will arise. A local reporter notices the contradictions.

choices.label: One universal message for all
choices.description: Stay consistent with a unified vision of development and good governance. Same message everywhere, same promises to all.
choices.feedback: Consistency builds trust. Voters notice that Arjun says the same thing in the slum as he does in the posh colony. 'This one doesn't change his colour,' an old shopkeeper tells his neighbours approvingly.

choices.label: Listen first, then respond
choices.description: Conduct genuine listening sessions — jan sunwai style. Let people speak their problems before offering solutions.
choices.feedback: Voters are stunned — a politician who actually listens? Arjun sits for hours hearing grievances, taking notes. A viral video of him comforting a crying elderly woman earns millions of views. The campaign gains an authentic grassroots energy.

choices.label: Focus on youth vote through social media
choices.description: Skip the tedious door-to-door grind. Go full digital — Instagram reels, YouTube shorts, Twitter spaces. Reach lakhs from your phone.
choices.feedback: Your social media game is fire! Arjun's reels trend on Instagram. Young voters are excited. But the older generation — the ones who actually vote in large numbers — feel ignored. Suresh Kumar shakes his head disapprovingly.

base_rounds.title: The Scandal
base_rounds.story: Breaking news at the worst possible time! A photograph surfaces showing Arjun at a lavish party three years ago, standing next to Vikram Malhotra — a controversial businessman under investigation for a land scam. The opponent's media machine goes into overdrive. #ArjunExposed trends on Twitter within hours. News channels run the photo on loop with ominous background music. Arjun swears it was an innocent social gathering, but the damage is spreading fast. Your phone is ringing off the hook — journalists, party workers, donors — everyone wants answers.
base_rounds.goal: Handle the crisis and protect the campaign's credibility
base_rounds.image_prompt: Indian campaign war room in crisis mode, people on phones looking stressed, TV screens showing breaking news with a controversial photo, newspapers scattered, tense atmosphere with dramatic red-tinged lighting, cinematic political thriller illustration
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Your silence was deafening. The media declared the candidate compromised. 'If he has nothing to hide, why won't he speak?' asks every news anchor. Voters start having serious doubts.

choices.label: Immediate press conference — full transparency
choices.description: Call a press conference within the hour. Show all evidence, explain the context, answer every question. Hide nothing.
choices.feedback: Arjun faces the cameras with calm confidence. He explains the context, shows he had no business dealings with Malhotra, and challenges anyone to prove otherwise. The transparency wins respect. Narrative shifts within 24 hours.

choices.label: Counter-attack with opponent's scandals
choices.description: The best defense is a good offense. Release a dossier of Sanjay Rao's own scandals — land grabs, nepotism, shell companies.
choices.feedback: The counter-attack lands hard! Rao's team scrambles to respond to their own scandal dump. Media is now covering both stories. The news cycle moves on, but you've established that your campaign fights dirty when provoked.

choices.label: Ignore it and stay on message
choices.description: Don't dignify the attack with a response. Keep campaigning on issues. Let the truth speak for itself.
choices.feedback: A risky gamble. Either the story dies on its own and you look dignified... or the silence is interpreted as guilt and the narrative takes root in voter minds. Only time will tell.

choices.label: Legal notice to media outlets
choices.description: Send defamation notices to channels running the story without verification. Show you mean business.
choices.feedback: Legal notices silence some smaller outlets, but major channels call it 'an attempt to muzzle the press.' Nisha warns you that antagonizing journalists during an election campaign is a dangerous game.

base_rounds.title: The Debate
base_rounds.story: The big night is here. A live televised debate between Arjun Mehta and Sanjay Rao, hosted by the city's most-watched news channel. 30 million viewers expected across the state. You've prepped Arjun for 72 straight hours — mock debates, rapid-fire Q&A, body language coaching. But Sanjay Rao is a seasoned debater who has demolished opponents on live TV before. The green room is tense. Arjun reviews his notes one last time. The moderator calls them to the stage. The red light on the camera blinks on.
base_rounds.goal: Win the televised debate and shift momentum
base_rounds.image_prompt: Dramatic Indian televised election debate, two candidates at podiums on a lit stage, TV cameras and bright studio lights, large audience seated, moderator at center desk, intense atmosphere with red and blue stage lighting, cinematic political illustration

choices.label: Aggressive attack strategy
choices.description: Go on the offensive from minute one. Interrupt, challenge, corner Rao on his record. Make him defend, not attack.
choices.feedback: Arjun comes out swinging! 'Where did ₹200 crore of development funds go?' The audience gasps. Rao is visibly flustered. But some viewers feel Arjun was 'too aggressive' and 'disrespectful to a senior leader.'

choices.label: Policy-focused, statesmanlike
choices.description: Win on substance. Present detailed policy proposals, cite data, let the ideas speak louder than personality attacks.
choices.feedback: Arjun presents a masterclass in policy debate. His 5-point development plan trends on social media. Academics and editorial boards praise him. 'This is how democracy should work,' writes a senior journalist. Rao's personal attacks look petty by comparison.

choices.label: Connect emotionally with audience
choices.description: Make it personal. Share real stories of real people. Make viewers see themselves in Arjun's struggle.
choices.feedback: When Arjun talks about the auto-rickshaw driver who can't afford his daughter's college fees, the studio audience falls silent. He looks directly into the camera and says, 'This election is about your family.' Phones light up with supportive messages.

choices.label: Use humor to disarm opponent
choices.description: Deploy wit and well-timed humor to create viral moments. Make Rao look out-of-touch while Arjun looks relatable.
choices.feedback: Arjun's one-liner — 'Rao sahab has been in power so long, he thinks the constituency is his ancestral property' — goes mega-viral. Memes flood the internet. But humor is a double-edged sword... will voters see wit or disrespect?

base_rounds.title: The Coalition Dilemma

ai_generation_context.context: Mid-campaign phase. The player is managing an underdog election campaign in India. A coalition opportunity or political alliance dilemma arises that forces the player to balance party unity, voter approval, and credibility. The candidate Arjun Mehta is idealistic while the opponent Sanjay Rao is a powerful incumbent.

base_rounds.image_prompt: a vibrant, bustling market square filled with colorful stalls, vendors negotiating loudly, bright banners fluttering in the breeze, warm sunlight casting playful shadows

base_rounds.title: Money Troubles
base_rounds.story: The campaign treasury is running dangerously low. Sanjay Rao is outspending you 4:1 on television ads — his face is on every hoarding, every bus stop, every newspaper. Your social media reach is good but TV still rules in Tier-2 India. Then a call comes in: Rajesh Agarwal, a wealthy real estate developer, offers ₹50 Lakhs for the campaign. The catch? He wants 'influence' — a promise that land regulations will be 'reviewed' if Arjun wins. Arjun doesn't know about the call yet.
base_rounds.goal: Solve the funding crisis without compromising the campaign
base_rounds.image_prompt: Tense meeting in a dimly lit Indian office, a wealthy businessman in expensive suit sliding an envelope across the table to a conflicted campaign manager, moral dilemma atmosphere, campaign posters visible on walls behind, dramatic chiaroscuro lighting, cinematic illustration

choices.label: Accept the donation — with conditions
choices.description: Take the money, give vague assurances, figure out the ethics later. You can't win without funds.
choices.feedback: The money flows in and the campaign machine roars back to life. New TV ads, bigger rallies, professional operations. But you know this comes with strings attached. Arjun senses something is off. And Rajesh Agarwal has a long memory.

choices.label: Reject and launch crowdfunding
choices.description: Refuse the tainted money and launch a public crowdfunding campaign instead. Let the people fund their own candidate.
choices.feedback: 'Arjun Mehta Rejects Crony Money — Launches People's Fund!' The crowdfunding page raises ₹15 Lakhs in 48 hours. Small donations of ₹100, ₹500, ₹1000 pour in. Each donation is a vote of confidence. The campaign becomes a movement.

choices.label: Accept but disclose publicly
choices.description: Take the donation but declare it publicly with full transparency. No backroom deals, everything on record.
choices.feedback: A rare move in Indian politics — accepting money with full public disclosure. The media is impressed. Some question why a developer is donating, but you've insulated yourself with transparency. Rajesh Agarwal is not happy about the publicity.

choices.label: Cut campaign costs dramatically
choices.description: Cancel expensive rallies, reduce staff, go lean. Run a tight ship with whatever you have left.
choices.feedback: The belt-tightening is brutal. Two volunteers quit. Rallies are smaller. But you're forced to be creative — WhatsApp campaigning, cycle rallies, and nukkad nataks become your weapons. Sometimes constraints breed innovation.

base_rounds.title: Election Week
base_rounds.story: The final week. Polls show it's neck and neck — Arjun 44%, Sanjay Rao 46%, undecided 10%. Your candidate is exhausted, running on chai and adrenaline. The opponent launches a devastating last-minute attack ad — dark imagery, ominous voiceover, questioning Arjun's 'real intentions.' Voters are jittery. The undecided 10% will decide everything. Every decision in the next 7 days could swing the election. This is it — the last push.
base_rounds.goal: Execute the final campaign strategy to win undecided voters
base_rounds.image_prompt: Intense Indian election campaign final week, exhausted but determined campaign team in war room late at night, charts showing close poll numbers on whiteboard, multiple TV screens showing news coverage, empty chai cups everywhere, dramatic tension, cinematic illustration
base_rounds.timeout_feedback: The campaign stalled in the final stretch. No clear closing message, no final push. Momentum died. Opponent's team smells blood and doubles their attacks. You've left the door wide open.

choices.label: Massive ground game — booth management
choices.description: Deploy workers at every polling booth. Voter lists, vehicle arrangements, phone banking — the whole election-day machinery.
choices.feedback: Suresh Kumar takes charge like a general commanding troops. Every booth has a panna pramukh, every voter has received a personal call. On election day, your booth-level management will be the envy of every campaign in the state.

choices.label: Viral social media campaign
choices.description: One final viral push — a powerful video, an emotional appeal, a hashtag that captures the nation's imagination.
choices.feedback: Nisha produces a 3-minute video — 'The India We Deserve' — featuring real voters talking about their hopes. It crosses 50 million views in 48 hours. Even people outside the constituency share it. Bollywood actors retweet. The momentum is undeniable.

choices.label: Personal appeal by candidate
choices.description: Arjun goes door-to-door himself for the final week. No rally, no media — just him, the voters, and genuine conversation.
choices.feedback: Arjun walks 15 km a day through every gali and mohalla. He sits on charpoys, drinks chai with strangers, listens to grandmothers. A photo of him helping carry a disabled voter's groceries becomes the defining image of the campaign.

choices.label: Celebrity endorsements and rallies
choices.description: Bring in big names — film stars, cricketers, social media influencers — for star-studded final rallies.
choices.feedback: A famous actor arrives for the final rally and the crowd goes wild! Selfies, autographs, massive media coverage. But cynics ask — are voters choosing a candidate or a celebrity? Still, the energy is electric.

base_rounds.title: Election Day
base_rounds.story: Polling day. The machines are beeping across 450 booths. Voters queue in the scorching heat, some waiting over two hours. By noon, turnout is at 45% — higher than expected. Reports of irregularities trickle in from 3 booths in Ward 12 — voters claim they were turned away. Exit polls start flashing contradictory predictions on TV. By 6 PM, voting ends. The tension is unbearable. You sit in the war room surrounded by empty chai cups and nervous volunteers, watching results trickle in booth by booth. Arjun paces by the window, phone in hand. Tomorrow, everything changes.
base_rounds.goal: Navigate election day and prepare for results
base_rounds.image_prompt: Indian election day scene, long queue of diverse voters outside a polling booth decorated with Election Commission banners, security personnel standing guard, bright sunlight casting long shadows, anticipation and democracy in action, vibrant cinematic illustration

choices.label: Ensure fair counting process
choices.description: Deploy your best people as counting agents. Document everything. Ensure not a single vote is miscounted or disputed.
choices.feedback: Your meticulous counting agents catch three discrepancies that would have cost you 800 votes. The Election Commission officers are impressed by your team's professionalism. 'This is how democracy should work,' the Returning Officer remarks.

choices.label: Mobilize last-minute voters
choices.description: Your data shows 15,000 of your supporters haven't voted yet. Send vehicles, make calls, get them to the booths before closing time.
choices.feedback: An all-out voter mobilization operation! Auto-rickshaws ferry elderly voters, volunteers make 5,000 phone calls in the last 3 hours. By closing time, turnout in your stronghold wards hits 78% — significantly above the constituency average.

choices.label: Media management for results night
choices.description: Prepare your media strategy — talking points for win or loss, spokespeople for TV channels, social media response team on standby.
choices.feedback: Win or lose, you're prepared. Nisha has talking points for every scenario, three spokespeople briefed for different channels, and a social media war room ready. When the first trends emerge, your narrative is already in place before the opponent can react.

choices.label: Stay calm, trust the process
choices.description: You've done everything possible. Now let democracy do its work. Gather the team, share a meal, and wait with dignity.
choices.feedback: Arjun gathers the entire team — volunteers, party workers, even the chai wallah who kept everyone fueled for 3 months. 'Whatever happens tomorrow, we fought with honour,' he says. The room erupts in applause. This was always about more than just winning.

crisis_events.title: Opposition Dirty Tricks!
crisis_events.description: Sanjay Rao's team has distributed thousands of fake pamphlets across slum areas — printed to look like official campaign material from Arjun's party — promising free liquor and cash for votes. The Election Commission is being alerted, and reporters are already asking questions. The pamphlets have your party's logo and Arjun's photo. This could destroy your credibility overnight.

choices.label: File complaint with Election Commission
choices.description: Go through the proper legal channel. File a formal complaint with evidence of the fake pamphlets.
choices.feedback: The Election Commission takes your complaint seriously. They issue a notice to the opponent's campaign. The story becomes about Rao's dirty tactics instead of Arjun's fake promises. Justice is slow but credible.

choices.label: Counter with truth campaign
choices.description: Launch an immediate counter-campaign — print your own pamphlets exposing the forgery, go on social media, and turn the dirty trick into a story about the opponent's desperation.
choices.feedback: Within hours, your team produces a viral video comparing the fake pamphlets with real ones, exposing the forgery. #FakePamphletScam trends nationally. The opponent's dirty trick backfires spectacularly.

crisis_events.title: Communal Tension!
crisis_events.description: Religious tensions erupt in a key constituency ward after a dispute over a religious procession route. Both sides are trying to use it politically — Rao's team is quietly communalizing the issue through WhatsApp forwards, while hardliners in your own party want Arjun to 'pick a side.' The situation is volatile. Police have been deployed. Any wrong move could trigger violence — or cost you an entire vote bank.

choices.label: Call for peace and unity
choices.description: Arjun personally visits the area, meets leaders from both communities, and issues a joint peace appeal. Rise above petty politics.
choices.feedback: Arjun's visit calms the situation. A photo of him standing between the two community leaders, hands joined, becomes iconic. National media praises his statesmanship. But some hardliners in the party feel he 'went soft' and grumble about loyalty.

choices.label: Stay neutral and let it blow over
choices.description: Don't get involved. This is a local dispute that could burn anyone who touches it. Let the administration handle it.
choices.feedback: Your absence is noted by both communities. 'Where was Arjun Mehta when our neighbourhood burned?' asks a community leader on TV. Rao's team uses the vacuum to position their candidate as 'the only one who showed up.' Silence has a cost.

crisis_events.title: Candidate Health Scare!
crisis_events.description: Arjun collapses during an afternoon rally in the sweltering heat! He's rushed to the district hospital in an ambulance. Media vans follow, cameras rolling. Within minutes, #ArjunHealth trends on Twitter. Rumors swirl — exhaustion, heart attack, food poisoning. The opposition whispers that he 'doesn't have the stamina for politics.' Doctors say he's severely dehydrated and needs 48 hours of rest — but that's 48 hours you don't have.

choices.label: Transparent health update
choices.description: Release complete medical reports, let Arjun address the public from his hospital bed via video. Full transparency about his condition.
choices.feedback: Arjun's honest video from the hospital — 'I'm human, I pushed too hard, but I'll be back fighting for you in 48 hours' — generates a wave of sympathy. Get-well-soon messages flood social media. Flowers arrive from rival party workers. Vulnerability becomes strength.

choices.label: Downplay and continue campaign
choices.description: Issue a brief statement about 'mild fatigue,' get Arjun back on his feet as soon as possible. The campaign can't afford to stop.
choices.feedback: Arjun is back at a rally the next morning, visibly pale but waving to the crowd. Party workers are inspired by his toughness. But doctors warn privately that he's pushing himself dangerously. And a leaked hospital photo contradicts the 'mild fatigue' narrative.

crisis_events.title: EVM Controversy!
crisis_events.description: One day before polling, allegations of EVM tampering explode on social media. A viral video — later proven to be from a different state and 2 years old — claims to show EVMs being loaded into an unauthorized vehicle. Panic spreads. Opposition parties demand paper ballots. The Election Commission issues a strong rebuttal but public trust is shaking. Your candidate must take a position.

choices.label: Demand independent audit
choices.description: Call for VVPAT verification of all machines in the constituency. Transparent, democratic, and reassures voters.
choices.feedback: Arjun's demand for a transparent audit is seen as principled and democratic. The Election Commission agrees to enhanced VVPAT verification in 5 booths. Voters feel reassured. National media covers it as an example of constructive opposition.

choices.label: Accept EC's assurance
choices.description: Trust the Election Commission's statement. Don't add fuel to the conspiracy fire. Focus on getting your voters to the booths.
choices.feedback: Your trust in institutions is seen as mature by some and naive by others. Some supporters feel you should have 'fought harder.' But the controversy dies down quickly and your campaign stays focused on the final push.

interdependencies.message: Low credibility is costing you votes! Voters don't trust a candidate with a questionable reputation.
Strong media presence is boosting voter awareness! Your candidate's name is on everyone's lips.
Party infighting is causing donors to pull back! Nobody wants to fund a campaign at war with itself.
Running out of money means fewer ads and events! The campaign's visibility is dropping fast.

news_events.headline: By-election announced for Lok Sabha constituency after sitting MP's disqualification. Election Commission sets polling date.
First-time candidate Arjun Mehta launches campaign with massive rally. Thousands attend despite scorching heat.
Door-to-door campaigning heats up as both candidates take their message to the streets. Voter turnout expected to be high.
Controversy erupts over photographs linking newcomer candidate to business tycoon. Campaign denies any wrongdoing.
All eyes on tonight's televised debate — the most anticipated political face-off this constituency has ever seen.
Coalition talks intensify as smaller parties weigh their options. Kingmaker role up for grabs in tight contest.
Campaign spending under scrutiny as Election Commission tightens expenditure monitoring. Both sides accuse the other of overspending.
Final week frenzy! Exit polls show razor-thin margins. Every vote counts in what analysts call 'the election of the decade' for this constituency.

dynamic_news_rules.headline: Latest opinion poll: Newcomer candidate Arjun Mehta takes surprising lead over 3-term incumbent! Political upset brewing?
Questions raised about campaign ethics and candidate credibility. Voters express concerns over transparency.
Campaign spending reaches record levels for a single constituency. Election Commission orders detailed audit of all expenditures.
Social media makes this the most-watched local election in the country. National channels set up permanent studios in the constituency.

achievements.title: Landslide Victory
achievements.description: Win the election with overwhelming voter approval — a historic mandate

achievements.title: Clean Campaign
achievements.description: Maintain exceptional credibility throughout the entire campaign

achievements.title: Media Master
achievements.description: Achieve dominant media coverage that shapes the election narrative

achievements.title: Party Whip
achievements.description: Keep the party united and fully behind the candidate through thick and thin

achievements.title: Grassroots Hero
achievements.description: Build strong voter approval through genuine grassroots connection

achievements.title: Campaign Veteran
achievements.description: Survive the entire campaign without losing voter support entirely

endings.title: Historic Victory 🏆
endings.description: Your candidate wins by a historic margin! The media calls it 'the people's revolution.' Arjun Mehta enters parliament as a symbol of hope and clean politics. Political analysts will study this campaign for decades. The victory speech at the town square — where it all began — draws tears from battle-hardened journalists. You did it. Against all odds, against the machine, against the money. Democracy won tonight.

endings.title: Narrow Win 🗳️
endings.description: Razor-thin margin! Just 2,847 votes separate victory from defeat. Every single decision you made — every rally, every media move, every crisis response — mattered. Arjun wins, but the opposition promises to make governance a nightmare. The celebrations are muted, the challenges ahead immense. But a win is a win. The underdog prevailed.

endings.title: Moral Victory ⭐
endings.description: You lost the election, but won hearts across the nation. Your clean, issue-based campaign inspired a generation of young Indians to believe in honest politics. Arjun's concession speech — gracious, dignified, and powerful — goes viral globally. 'We didn't win the seat, but we won something more important: we proved that politics doesn't have to be dirty.' Arjun vows to return stronger. And everyone believes him.

endings.title: Scandal Ridden 📰
endings.description: The campaign imploded under the weight of scandals, contradictions, and poor crisis management. What began as a hopeful revolution ended in embarrassment. Arjun finishes a distant third, behind even the independent candidate. Media postmortems are brutal. 'The campaign that promised transparency delivered only chaos,' writes a columnist. Time to update your resume and maybe switch careers entirely.

endings.title: Party Split 💔
endings.description: Internal conflicts tore the campaign apart from the inside. Key supporters defected to the opponent. Party workers leaked strategy documents to the media. Volunteers stopped showing up. The candidate was fighting two enemies — the opponent outside and the infighting within. Sanjay Rao didn't even need to campaign hard in the final weeks. Your own team did his work for him.

random_events.title: Endorsement Surprise!
random_events.text: A popular local leader — a retired school principal beloved by the entire constituency — unexpectedly endorses Arjun Mehta at a community gathering! 'This young man reminds me of the leaders we once had — honest, passionate, and genuinely caring,' she tells the crowd. The endorsement carries enormous weight in the community.

random_events.title: Monsoon Rally Washout!
random_events.text: Heavy unseasonal rains cancel a major rally that took weeks to organize. Thousands of supporters who traveled from rural areas get drenched. The stage collapses, sound equipment is damaged, and the media captures footage of soggy banners and disappointed faces. Nature doesn't care about your campaign schedule. ₹3,000 worth of equipment and logistics down the drain.

how_to_play: You are the campaign manager for Arjun Mehta, a first-time candidate challenging a powerful 3-term incumbent. Every decision affects your resources: Voter Approval, Campaign Fund, Media Coverage, Party Unity, and Credibility.

Talk to NPCs for advice — Arjun can share his vision and values, Nisha Sharma knows media strategy, and Suresh Kumar understands the dirty realities of election politics. Build trust with them for better guidance.
Some rounds are timed! When the timer appears, make quick decisions or face consequences. In real campaigns, delayed responses to crises can be fatal.
Watch for crisis events that appear randomly — scandals, dirty tricks, and controversies require immediate attention. Your opponent Sanjay Rao is always looking for an opening to exploit.
Balance idealism with pragmatism. Running a perfectly clean campaign is noble but may not win votes. Winning through questionable means damages your credibility. Find your path.
learning_objectives: Understand the mechanics of democratic elections — campaigning, coalition-building, media management, and voter outreach in the Indian political context.
Learn how to manage crises, scandals, and misinformation while maintaining credibility and public trust.
Appreciate the ethical dilemmas faced in political campaigns — the tension between winning and maintaining integrity.
Develop strategic thinking about resource allocation, communication, and decision-making under pressure and time constraints.

glossary_terms.definition: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement — your fallback if no deal is reached.
glossary_terms.example: If you can't agree on a price, you could sell to a different buyer — that's your BATNA.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: A strong BATNA gives negotiating power. Knowing both parties' BATNAs reveals who needs the deal more.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: A job applicant with another offer has a stronger BATNA and can negotiate more confidently.

glossary_terms.definition: Finding solutions where both parties gain value rather than one side winning at the other's expense.
glossary_terms.example: Agreeing on a payment plan that works for both buyer and seller, rather than a discount that hurts profit.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Integrative negotiation expands the 'pie' by identifying trade-offs where each party values things differently.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Labor-management negotiations that increase productivity in exchange for better wages can benefit both sides.

glossary_terms.definition: Setting an initial reference point in a negotiation that influences the final outcome.
glossary_terms.example: The first price mentioned in a negotiation becomes the anchor around which all counteroffers are compared.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research shows people are heavily influenced by the first number they hear, even when irrelevant.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Salary negotiations: starting with a high number tends to result in higher final offers.
